This page brings together everything Digital Humanities at the University of Bern offers in the spring semester 2027 (FS 2027): seminars and colloquia, the online lecture, the workshops of the *Applied Digital Humanities* modules, and the meetings for students in their final year and in the doctoral programme.

- **Lecture period:** 22 February – 4 June 2027
- **Easter break:** 26 March – 4 April 2027 (no teaching)
- **Whit Monday:** 17 May 2027 (no teaching)
- **Registration:** all courses are booked via [KSL](https://www.ksl.unibe.ch/KSL/home); the course number is given for each course. Course material is made available on [ILIAS](https://ilias.unibe.ch/).
- **Questions about the study programmes:** Adrian Demleitner, head of study programmes ([adrian.demleitner@unibe.ch](mailto:adrian.demleitner@unibe.ch))

::: {.callout-note}
There is no DH Lab in the spring semester. The final-year meetings take place as separate dates (see [below](#final-year-and-doctoral-programme)).
:::

## Course descriptions

::: {.callout-note title="First draft"}
The descriptions below are drafts. The descriptions in KSL are binding.
:::

### Building and Assessing Bots for Research in the Humanities
*Colloquium · 3 ECTS · Tobias Hodel · Mondays 10:00–12:00 from 8 March, full-day block on 3 May, presentations in the following weeks*

Chatbots based on large language models are becoming part of how students and researchers search for, read and summarise historical information. Starting from the pilot project *Swiss History Bot*, the colloquium asks whether a chatbot can become a source-traceable research tool. Participants **build** bots on a curated corpus (HLS, Dodis, infoclio.ch, e-periodica), combining a knowledge graph with a vector database (GraphRAG) and running on the University of Bern's own LLM infrastructure, and **assess** them: is every claim traceable to a source, how often does the bot hallucinate (curated test set), and is it useful for students, teachers and researchers?

### Eine Stadt analysieren: Stadtgeschichte Aarau (Bild und Text)
*Seminar · 6 ECTS · Tobias Hodel · in German · two online sessions, two full days, presentations*

Digital and public history through a project, in collaboration with the authors of the *Stadtgeschichte Aarau*. Students work with sources on the population (address books, resident registers, census data, city maps) and on public discourse (*Aarauer Neujahrsblätter* on e-periodica). No programming skills are needed; some Python is introduced. Students deliver a group presentation, an individual handout (4–5 pages) and a blog post on their project for a wider audience; the grade is the average of all parts.

### Text Recognition: Dealing with Text Programmatically
*Seminar · 6 ECTS · Tobias Hodel · Wednesdays 13:00–17:00, seven sessions from 7 April to 2 June*

An introduction to automated text recognition: the basics of OCR and HTR (pipeline, CER/WER metrics), eScriptorium and Kraken, open models and HTR-United, as well as TrOCR and vision-language models (GPT-4o, Gemini, open VLMs). The seminar is based on the open teaching resource [thodel.github.io/atr](https://thodel.github.io/atr/) (CC BY 4.0), with quiz and literature list, and on the open-access book *Automated Text Recognition* (Schonhardt, Geelhaar, Hodel, Odstrčilík; Bielefeld University Press, 2026).

### From Information to Insights: Introduction to Data Analysis Using Open Data
*Seminar · 6 ECTS · Francesco Beretta · Tuesdays 10:15–12:00, weekly*

An introduction to data analysis with open data: from finding and preparing information to deriving insights. *Description to follow.*

### Research Perspectives on Born-Digital
*Colloquium · 3 ECTS · Critical Algorithm Studies · with Digital History · Moritz Mähr, Adrian Demleitner, Daniel Gammenthaler, Max Frischknecht and others · Wednesday afternoons, weekly*

Current approaches and projects on researching born-digital artefacts in the Digital Humanities and Digital History. Inputs and guest lectures present recent and ongoing research on artefacts such as databases, video games and source code.

### Alt-Soc
*Microcourse · 0.5 ECTS · one half day · with Digital In/Justice*

*Description to follow.*

### Digital Humanities — Introductions
*Lecture · 3 ECTS · online only*

Seventeen researchers from Swiss and European universities present major research areas and methods of the Digital Humanities in recorded lectures, which can be worked through in any order. Assessment is an open-book multiple-choice exam. See the [course page](/content/intro-lecture/index.qmd).
